newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB affirms little inflation risk, generous policy.
newsitem.headline: SNB affirms little inflation risk, generous policy.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) affirmed that the risk of inflation in Switzerland is currently low and monetary supply would remain generous to create the monetary basis for economic recovery.

The SNB also repeated in its 1996 annual report that it was conscious it had to be very careful in picking the correct time for changing its policy regime if price stablity was to be maintained in the medium term.
"A change in monetary policy will therefore first become an issue when a recovery in the Swiss economy is perceptible," SNB said in a chapter on monetary policy.

In agreement with the Federal Council, the SNB said it was continuing its easy policy in 1997 and intended to continue to keep seasonally-adjusted central bank money above the medium-term target path.
"Thus we are taking into account the unfavourable economic situation and uncertainties stemming from European monetary integration," the SNB added.
Monetary policy for 1997 is based on the expectation that real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Switzerland would rise around 0.5 percent and inflation on average would be one percent.
"Demand for central bank money should only show weak growth under these preconditions," the SNB said.
However, the SNB also repeated that it retained the right to deviate from its course in the event of disturbances on financial markets.
